title: Operator Quick-Adjust: scaling slider presets, throughput charting, and immutable audit trail
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Add an 'Operator Quick-Adjust' panel to the Fleet Controls Console that groups three related capabilities: 1) compact scaling controls (slider + numeric presets + instant apply), 2) a throughput dashboard showing live QPS/TPS with p50/p95 latency overlays and capacity headroom, and 3) an immutable change history with operator identity, reason, and an easy rollback link. This is targeted at Dedicated customers who need fast manual interventions during traffic spikes while preserving auditability and SLA guarantees.

Goals:
- Enable SREs and operators to make rapid, low-risk scaling adjustments with clear feedback on expected throughput and cost impact.
- Surface throughput and latency signals tied to the selected capacity so operators can reason about trade-offs.
- Record all manual adjustments in an append-only change history that ties to SSO identity and includes optional freeform reason, linked PR/Runbook, and a one-click rollback where feasible.

Scope and non-goals:
- Includes the UI surface, telemetry hooks, and backend audit-write integration to Customer Events.
- Does NOT include new autoscaler algorithm changes; it surfaces and can trigger existing autoscaling policies (ENG work).
- Does NOT replace existing Fleet Presets; it introduces a complementary quick-presets UX for on-call scenarios.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Operator Quick-Adjust panel is visible to users with fleet-admin role.
- Slider and numeric presets apply changes to capacity manifest with preview showing estimated throughput and cost delta before commit.
- Throughput dashboard shows live throughput, 1m/5m/15m smoothing options, and latency p50/p95 lines; charts update within 5s.
- Every manual change creates an immutable audit record with: operator id, timestamp, old/new capacity, reason (optional), link to runbook or PR (optional). Audit entries are queryable by time range and operator.
- Rollback attempts to reapply the previous capacity manifest; if rollback fails, provide deterministic error and fallback suggestion.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Compact controls: a single slider for quick gestures and an inline numeric field for precise values. We considered a full modal flow but chose an inline compact panel to reduce time-to-action for on-call engineers.
- Preview vs. immediate apply: default to 'Preview' on first change per session to reduce accidental large scale-ups. Power users can enable 'Immediate apply' in preferences.
- Cost estimate: the estimator will use current pricing profile and model mix; this is approximate. We intentionally show a range (lower/upper bound) to avoid false precision.
- Audit immutability: audit entries are write-once to the events store. For private deployments that integrate with customer KMS or HSM, the console will still write audit metadata locally but recommend archiving to customer-specified logs.

Integration points / Implementation hints for ENG:
- API: POST /fleets/{id}/quick-adjust with payload {target_capacity, preview: bool, reason: string, runbook_url: string} and return estimated_throughput, estimated_cost_delta. (ENG to design exact contract).
- Telemetry: emit events.quick_adjust.request and events.quick_adjust.applied with operator, diff, and source (console/ui).
- Audit store: append-only event to audit service used by Private and Dedicated. Ensure consistent schema with existing audit queries (see ENG-56321).
- Charting: reuse existing throughput backend series endpoints but add ability to request series anchored to a proposed capacity to compute headroom overlays.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: operators may over-provision during traffic spikes causing cost overruns. Mitigation: require explicit two-step confirmation for changes > 2x current capacity unless Immediate Apply is enabled in user preferences, and show cost delta prominently.
- Risk: race with autoscaler. Mitigation: change record includes intent flag (manual_override) so autoscaler can be tuned to backoff for a short cooldown window.

Links to artifacts:
- PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRAPROD/pages/Quick-Adjust+PRD (internal)
- Mockups: https://drive.google.com/mockups/quick-adjust-v1 (design frames + interaction map)
- Backend ticket: ENG-56321 (throughput preview API)
- Related PM tickets: PM-281307 (fleet orchestration wizard), PM-45167 (capacity intent editor)

Release and rollout plan:
- Beta target to selected Dedicated customers in console-2026.03-beta. Start with canary cohort (3 tenants) for 2 weeks, collect telemetry on manual adjustments and rate of rollbacks, then full release.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Track time-to-apply for manual changes and rollback success rate.
- Add alert for unusually large number of quick-adjusts from a single operator (>5 in 10 minutes).

Notes for legal/compliance review:
- Audit trail must satisfy SOC2 evidence requirements. We flagged this to Security; they requested a policy review only if exportable audit snapshots are implemented (TBD).
comments: 2026-02-18 — Aisha Kumar: Created ticket after on-call incident where ops had to rapidly scale a Dedicated fleet and lacked a concise preview of throughput and cost. Link to incident notes: https://redwood.incidents/INC-1129

2026-02-21 — Marco Santos (assignee): Scoped initial API contract with ENG. We'll need a new endpoint for preview and a lightweight optimistic write path for manual applies. Blocking question posted to ENG-56321 thread.

2026-02-25 — Design review (Jia Li): Mockups v1 uploaded to Drive. Suggested adding 'safety band' visual on slider to indicate recommended range based on historical usage. Updated mockups: https://drive.google.com/mockups/quick-adjust-v1#frame=3

2026-03-02 — Eng sync (Nate O'Connor): Backend can support estimated_throughput but needs an efficient way to compute headroom without expensive re-sim. Proposed heuristic: use recent qps-to-gpu mapping + model profiles. ENG will deliver API by 2026-03-08 (ENG-56321).
2026-03-06 — PM note: Added requirement that large manual adjustments require secondary confirmation. Updated acceptance criteria accordingly.

2026-03-09 — QA (Simone Alvarez): End-to-end smoke tested on staging fleet. Chart refresh interval tuned to 5s to avoid flicker. Found an edge case where rollback did not restore autoscaler cooldown flag; added dependency ENG-59344 to address.

2026-03-10 — Marco Santos: Merged console-side feature branch to feature flag 'quick_adjust_v1' (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1287). Backend preview endpoint deployed to staging. Starting canary cohort configuration.
2026-03-10 — PM follow-up: Prepare operator playbook snippets describing recommended usage during traffic spikes; link to runbooks will be surfaced in the UI.
